title: About — BetterMapandan.org
description: About the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan, and the Better Mapandan civic transparency project.
body: About About Better Mapandan An independent civic transparency portal for the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "AboutPage", "name": "About Better Mapandan", "url": "https://bettermapandan.org/about/", "description": "Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities.", "mainEntity": { "@type": "WebSite", "name": "Better Mapandan", "url": "https://bettermapandan.org" } } About Mapandan The municipality History Mapandan was created as an independent pueblo on December 28, 1887, through Director General No. 39. After a period of financial insolvency (1905–1908) when it was re-absorbed into Mangaldan, the town was re-established as an independent municipality in 1909 under Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. The town was named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants in the area. Geography Mapandan is a third-class municipality in the province of Pangasinan, Philippines. It covers a land area of 32.92 km² and is composed of 15 barangays. The municipality is located in the western part of Pangasinan, bordered by the Lingayen Gulf to the north and the Agno River floodplain to the south. Population 38,228 PSA Census 2024 Land Area 32.92 km² MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Barangays 15 DILG / Comelec Cultural Heritage Local traditions and community life Pandan Festival Held annually during the second week of April, the Pandan Festival celebrates Mapandan's cultural heritage with street dancing, pageants, and community gatherings. Pandan Festival Town Plaza The historic center of Mapandan's community life and civic gatherings. Town Plaza Agriculture Rice fields and farmland across Mapandan's countryside — the agricultural heart of the municipality. Agriculture History Mapandan through the years 1887–1909 Founding & Early Governance From southern barrios of Mangaldan to an independent pueblo—and back again. Mapandan’s first two decades were defined by the courage of its founders, the fragility of a new town, and the determination to rise again. Read more Before 1887: Southern barrios of Mangaldan Before Mapandan existed as an independent pueblo, the area belonged to Mangaldan. The future municipality consisted of southern communities including Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac. The movement toward establishing a separate town was initiated by ten local leaders: Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, Andres Bongato, Ambrosio Calimlim, Valeriano Tamondong, Tomas Aquino, Fulgencio Nato, Filomeno Sarmiento, Jose Lalas, and Florencio Datuin. December 28, 1887: Mapandan becomes a pueblo Mapandan was established as an independent pueblo through Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, signed by Governor General Emilio Bravo. The new pueblo was initially composed of the southern barrios of Mangaldan: Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac. The first town center: Torres The first center of the new pueblo was in what is now Barangay Torres. The area had abundant pandan plants and was associated with a church where Fr. Jose Torres served as parish priest. However, the location proved inconvenient—too close to the southern boundary and too far from communities to the north. The center was eventually transferred to an area that had previously been a sitio of Apaya. Much of the land in the new Poblacion was owned by the Aquino family. Leon Hilario Aquino encouraged settlement by subdividing land into uniform lots and making them available to families. 1903: The epidemic An epidemic severely affected Mapandan, causing major population depletion, residents leaving the town, declining municipal resources, and a financial crisis. The 1903 census recorded Mapandan’s population at 4,198. 1905–1908: Return to Mangaldan Because of the population and financial problems caused by the epidemic, Mapandan was temporarily returned to its mother municipality, Mangaldan. 1909: Restoration Mapandan was formally re-established as a municipality under Executive Order No. 10, signed by Governor General James F. Smith. 1910s–1940s Agricultural Growth & Wartime After its restoration, Mapandan developed as a predominantly agricultural community. Farming remained central to the local economy, with rice becoming the municipality’s principal crop. The decades ahead would bring war, occupation, and the beginning of reconstruction. Read more Agricultural foundations Rice became the municipality’s principal crop and livestock raising developed as an important secondary livelihood. The municipality’s current seal still reflects these agricultural foundations through its rice, cattle, chicken and hog imagery. 1940s: War, occupation and rebuilding The Second World War interrupted the development of communities across Pangasinan. In the postwar years, Mapandan’s communities entered a period of reconstruction and social and economic change. The decades following the war also brought changes in landholding, agriculture, education and local community organization. 1940s–1970s Post-War Community Development After the war, Mapandan’s communities began to take shape. New barangays were formed, land ownership changed hands, and the municipality entered a period of organized community development. Read more Barangays begin taking shape Instead of only telling municipal history, the history of how Mapandan’s communities formed tells an equally important story. Sta. Maria — Formerly part of Luyan, developed from former hacienda land. Tenants gained opportunities to own the land they had been farming after the war. It became a separate barrio in 1965. Golden — Formerly Amanoaoac North, a sitio of Amanoaoac. Its name was associated with the Golden Distillery, which operated after liberation. Golden became a separate barangay in 1967. Torres — The first seat of Mapandan, which once contained several sitios that later developed into separate barangays. 1967–1973: Community development Golden was officially approved as a separate barangay in 1967. The community then underwent substantial development including road improvement, waterworks, school construction, sports facilities, cooperative organization, agricultural training, and sanitation programs. 1972 — Golden was recognized as a SEATO/PACD Model Village, receiving a national-level award presented in Malacañang on September 8, 1972. 1972–1973 — Coral became a barangay through Municipal Council Resolution No. 87 (May 4, 1972), Provincial Board Resolution No. 155 (August 10, 1972), and Proclamation No. 11 (April 25, 1973), followed by a special election for barangay officials on May 6, 1973. 1980s–2001 Modernization Mapandan’s population grew substantially, its services expanded, and infrastructure developed. The municipality moved from historical survival toward economic growth. Read more Population growth Mapandan’s population grew steadily through the second half of the 20th century: 20,094 in 1980, 25,622 in 1990, and 30,775 in 2000. Infrastructure and services The municipality expanded roads, schools, health facilities, and public services. Community organizations grew alongside the population. 2002–2024 21st Century Development From a new municipal classification to healthcare expansion and digital government—Mapandan enters the 21st century with growing services, cultural pride, and a more connected community. Read more 2002: A new municipal classification Mapandan was elevated to a third-class municipality. The municipality credits then-Mayor Jose Ferdinand Z. Calimlim Jr. with spearheading income and revenue-generation strategies that contributed to the municipality’s elevation. 2010s: Celebrating the Pandan heritage The Pandan Festival developed into an important annual celebration of Mapandan’s identity, culture and community. The 9th Pandan Festival was held alongside the town fiesta from March 11–19, 2018. 2017–2018: Early digital government efforts The municipal government began developing an online presence that made government information, public notices, disaster information and community announcements accessible through the web. 2022–2024: Expanding healthcare access National health infrastructure funding supported the development of the Mapandan Super Health Center. The 2022 General Appropriations Act included ₱6.5 million for the project. Its first phase was inaugurated on March 15, 2024, expanding access to laboratory, dental and primary healthcare services for residents of Mapandan and nearby communities. 2020s: Government services go digital Mapandan’s government information infrastructure increasingly incorporates digital channels, including information and access guidance for the national eGovPH platform. 2024: Mapandan today More than 130 years after its establishment as a pueblo, Mapandan is a 15-barangay municipality with a population of 38,228. Its history has been shaped by migration, agriculture, community organization, local government, cultural traditions and continuing investment in public services. ← 1 / 5 → Source: Mayor Karl Vega, “History of Mapandan” — YouTube Sources & Historical Notes Historical accounts drawn from municipal archives, provincial records, and published heritage studies of Pangasinan. Municipality of Mapandan — Municipal Profile Municipality of Mapandan — Physical Characteristics Philippine Statistics Authority — Mapandan PSGC Philippine News Agency — Super Health Center Inauguration Population Growth Mapandan through the census Population by census year Year Population 1903 4,198 1918 6,049 1939 7,286 1948 9,836 1960 13,065 1970 16,653 1980 20,094 1990 25,622 2000 30,775 2010 34,439 2020 38,058 2024 38,228 Source: Philippine Statistics Authority, Census of Population (1903–2024) About the Project What is Better Mapandan? Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities. Our Mission To make government information accessible, understandable, and actionable for every Mapandan resident. We believe that open data strengthens democracy and empowers communities to participate meaningfully in local governance. How It Works We compile publicly available government data — from COA audit reports, PSA census data, municipal disclosures, and provincial issuances — into a single, easy-to-navigate website. Every piece of information is sourced and attributed. Open Source The source code is publicly available. Developers can contribute, audit, and improve the platform. View on GitHub → Independent Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. It is not an official government website and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. Volunteer-Run Built and maintained entirely by volunteers. No government funding is used. Cost to the people of Mapandan: ₱0. Contribute Get involved Better Mapandan thrives on community participation. Here's how you can help: Report Incorrect Information Spotted an error? Help us keep the data accurate by reporting mistakes. Report an error → Contribute Code Developers can contribute features, fix bugs, or improve accessibility on GitHub. Fork on GitHub → Verify Data Help verify government information by cross-referencing with official sources. Submit verification → Share with Residents Spread the word about Better Mapandan so more residents can access government information. Disclaimer Important notice Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. It is not an official government website and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. Information presented on this site is compiled from publicly available government sources and community research. While we strive for accuracy, we cannot guarantee the completeness or timeliness of all data. For official government information, please visit mapandan.gov.ph or contact the municipal government directly.

Covering 32.92 square kilometres, around three-quarters of its land supports agriculture — mainly rice, alongside corn, livestock, and seasonal vegetables. The municipal administration operates under the tagline “Kaakibat niyo ang Aktibo at Responsableng Liderato” (Partnering with you in Active and Responsible Leadership). 01 Founded Dec. 28, 1887 Separated from Mangaldan as an independent pueblo under Governor General Emilio Bravo, led by ten local leaders including Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, and Andres Bongato. 02 Re-established 1909 A severe epidemic forced temporary re-annexation to Mangaldan. Full autonomy was restored via Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. 03 Agricultural heart Approximately 75% of the municipality's 32.92 km² is dedicated to lowland crop production, livestock, and poultry farming. Leadership Currently in office Hon. title: Accessibility Statement — BetterMapandan.org
description: Accessibility commitment and standards for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Support Accessibility Statement Our commitment to making government information accessible to all residents. Our commitment Better Mapandan is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We continually improve the user experience for everyone and apply the relevant accessibility standards. Conformance Status We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at the AA level. These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible for people with disabilities. Measures Taken We have implemented the following accessibility features across the site: Semantic HTML structure Skip-to-content navigation link Visible focus indicators Sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 minimum) Keyboard-accessible navigation Screen-reader-friendly labels Descriptive link text Proper heading hierarchy Accessibility features Keyboard Navigation All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard. Use Tab to move between elements, Enter to activate links and buttons, and Escape to close overlays. Screen Readers The site uses semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and proper heading hierarchy to ensure screen readers can navigate the content effectively. Color & Contrast All text meets WCAG AA contrast requirements. Information is never conveyed through color alone — icons, labels, and text are always provided alongside color coding. Text Resizing The site uses relative units (rem, em) for text sizing. Users can resize text up to 200% without loss of content or functionality. Forms All form inputs are associated with labels. Error messages are descriptive and programmatically associated with the relevant input fields. Tables Data tables include proper header associations ( <th scope> ), captions where appropriate, and are responsive on mobile devices. Known limitations We are aware of the following accessibility limitations and are working to address them: PDF documents: Some linked government documents (COA reports, provincial issuances) may not be fully accessible. We provide HTML summaries where possible. Interactive maps: The Leaflet map is navigable via keyboard but may present challenges for screen reader users. We provide alternative text descriptions and a data table fallback. Third-party content: Embedded content from external government websites may not meet the same accessibility standards. Feedback We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of Better Mapandan. If you encounter accessibility barriers, please let us know: Report an Issue Use our reporting form to describe the accessibility issue, the page URL, and your browser/device information. Report accessibility issue → GitHub Issues Developers can file accessibility issues directly on our GitHub repository. Open GitHub issue →

No. Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. It is not an official government website and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. For official information, visit mapandan.gov.ph . How is this project funded? Better Mapandan is entirely volunteer-run and uses no government funding. The cost to the people of Mapandan is ₱0. Hosting and domain costs are covered by the BetterGov.ph initiative. Where does the data come from? All data is compiled from publicly available government sources: COA audit reports, PSA census data, DILG Full Disclosure filings , BLGF treasury data, provincial issuances, and municipal announcements. Every source is attributed on the page where the data appears. How do I report incorrect information? Visit our Report Incorrect Information page. Provide the page URL, the specific error, and the correct information if known. Our volunteers will review and update the data. Services Government services How do I get a birth certificate? Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) at the 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion. Bring a valid ID and the required fee. Processing time is typically 3–5 working days. See the full requirements on the Birth Certificate service page . How do I apply for a business permit? Visit the Municipal Treasurer's Office (MTO) with your DTI/SEC registration, barangay clearance, and other required documents. New permits are processed in 3–5 working days. See the Business Permit service page for full details. How do I get a building permit? Apply through the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO). Building permits require a zoning clearance, architectural plans, and structural plans. Processing takes 10–15 working days. See the Building Permit service page . How do I request a barangay clearance? Visit your barangay hall with a valid ID. Barangay clearances are typically issued the same day. This is often a prerequisite for other government transactions. Data & Transparency Data questions What does "Placeholder" mean on data? Some data is marked as "Placeholder" when the exact figure is not yet available from official sources. We use reasonable estimates based on available data and clearly mark these so residents know the difference between verified and estimated figures. How often is the data updated? Each data section includes a "Last updated" timestamp. Major updates happen when new COA audit reports, PSA census data, or municipal financial disclosures become available. The site is continuously improved by volunteers. Can I download the data? Yes. The Statistics page includes CSV download options for chart data. The Transparency page provides links to source documents. All data is publicly available and free to reuse under open data principles. How can I verify the data myself? Every data section includes a source attribution and, where available, a link to the original document. You can cross-reference with official sources like the COA website, PSA, or the municipal government directly. Contact Still have questions? For government services Contact the relevant office directly. See the Government Directory for phone numbers and email addresses. For this website Report issues, suggest improvements, or contribute on GitHub . For data corrections, use the Report Incorrect Information form.

title: Privacy Policy — BetterMapandan.org
description: Privacy policy for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Legal Privacy Policy How we handle data on the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal. Overview Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. It is not an official government website and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. We collect minimal data and are committed to protecting your privacy. Information We Collect Automatically collected: When you visit Better Mapandan, our hosting provider (GitHub Pages) may collect standard web server logs including your IP address, browser type, referring URL, and pages visited. This is standard server operation and is not used to identify individual visitors. Search queries: The search functionality runs entirely in your browser. Your search queries are never sent to a server or stored. Language preference: If you use the language switcher (when available), your preference is stored locally in your browser and is never transmitted to us. How We Use Information We do not use, sell, or share personal information. Server logs are used only for maintaining the website and understanding usage patterns in aggregate. Cookies Better Mapandan does not use cookies. The language preference is stored using localStorage , which is a browser-only storage mechanism and is not transmitted to any server. Third-Party Services The site loads the following external resources: Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) — for font loading Open-Meteo API (open-meteo.com) — for weather data (loaded only on the homepage) Leaflet / OpenStreetMap — for the interactive map (loaded only on the homepage) These services have their own privacy policies. We do not share any personal data with them. Data Sources All government data presented on this site is compiled from publicly available official sources. This data is already public and is presented here for informational purposes. Changes to This Policy This privacy policy may be updated from time to time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date. Contact For privacy-related inquiries, please open an issue on our GitHub repository or use the report form .

NTA/IRA Dependency 82–87% Of total operating revenue comes from the National Tax Allocation (formerly IRA). Locally generated taxes cover only a small fraction of municipal operations. Verified Source: BLGF / COA AAR 20% Development Fund 20% Of annual NTA share is earmarked for social development, economic development, and environmental management projects under Section 287 of R.A. 7160. Restricted to capital works; cannot fund personal services. Statutory 5% LDRRMF 5% Of estimated regular annual revenues allocated for disaster preparedness under R.A. 10121. Split: 30% Quick Response Fund (emergency relief) + 70% pre-disaster preparedness and mitigation. Statutory Special Education Fund (SEF) Financed through a 1% tax levy on assessed real property values under Section 235 of R.A. 7160. Co-administered by the Municipal School Board. Restricted to supplementary funding for public schools: facility construction, educational materials, instructional support, and sports development. Statutory Personnel Services Cap Section 325(a) of R.A. 7160 limits total personnel spending to 45% or 55% of total annual regular income depending on LGU classification. Mapandan has reduced PS from 51% of operating income (CY 2013) to under 42% (CY 2015), ensuring compliance. title: Agriculture Subsidy
body: Agriculture Agricultural Subsidies Apply for agricultural subsidies in Mapandan. Seeds at 50% discount, plus technical assistance and livestock services. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Agricultural Subsidies", "description": "The Municipal Agriculture Office provides subsidized agricultural programs including seeds (hybrid and inbred at 50% DA-RFU subsidy), fertilizers, farm equipment, and technical assistance. Also provides seed certification, crop protection services, and animal anti-rabies vaccination.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Agriculture", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) provides various government-subsidized agricultural programs to support local farmers and fisherfolk in Mapandan. These programs include subsidies for seeds, fertilizers, farm equipment, and technical assistance to improve agricultural productivity and livelihood. Availability of subsidies depends on national and provincial funding allocations. Requirements Farmer registration with the Municipal Agriculture Office Barangay certification of residency and farming activity Farm location and land area information Procedure Register with the Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) as a farmer or fisherfolk. Secure a barangay certification confirming your farming activity and residency. Submit your registration and requirements to the MAO. Wait for availability announcement of agricultural subsidies or programs. Receive agricultural assistance or subsidies upon program approval. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: Varies (depends on availability) Fee: Free (government-subsidized) Where to Apply: Municipal Agriculture Office, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1873 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Aics
body: Social Welfare — IDs & Certifications AICS Assistance Apply for Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) in Mapandan. Learn about requirements, eligibility, and how to get help from the MSWDO. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "AICS Assistance", "description": "Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) is a government program that provides financial assistance to individuals and families facing emergencies such as medical crises, bereavement, or other unforeseen circumstances. In Mapandan, AICS assistance is administered by the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) in coordination with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD).", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Social Welfare — IDs & Certifications", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) is a government program that provides financial assistance to individuals and families facing emergencies such as medical crises, bereavement, or other unforeseen circumstances. In Mapandan, AICS assistance is administered by the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) in coordination with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD). Requirements Barangay certification stating the resident’s crisis situation Medical certificate (for medical-related assistance) Death certificate (for burial assistance) Valid government-issued ID Case study or social worker assessment Procedure Secure a barangay certification from your barangay captain or kagawad. Gather all required documents (medical certificate, death certificate, etc.). Visit the MSWDO office and submit your application with supporting documents. Wait for the social worker’s assessment and case study. Receive financial assistance upon approval of your application. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 1–3 working days Fee: Free Where to Apply: MSWDO Office, Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1751 / 0930-641-3934 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Birth Certificate
body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Birth Certificate Request a birth certificate from the Mapandan MCR. Standard ₱115, late registration ₱315–₱1,015. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Birth Certificate", "description": "A birth certificate is a vital record issued by the Municipal Civil Registrar. Covers standard registration (₱115), registration by unmarried parents (₱215), hospital registration (₱100), and late registration (₱315–₱1,015 depending on age). Late registration requires 10-day posting period.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Civil Registry & Vital Records", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description A birth certificate is a vital record that serves as proof of identity, age, and Filipino citizenship. The Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) of Mapandan issues certified copies of locally registered birth certificates. This document is required for school enrollment, passport application, employment, and other legal purposes. Requirements Valid government-issued ID of the requesting party PSA copy of the birth certificate (if available, for verification) Barangay certification of residency (for the person named on the certificate) Affidavit of two disinterested persons (required for delayed registration only) Procedure Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office and present valid identification. Fill out the request form and provide the necessary supporting documents. Pay the certification fee at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Receive the certified birth certificate upon release. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 10 minutes (standard) to 10+ days (late registration) Fee: ₱115 (standard) / ₱215 (unmarried) / ₱100 (hospital) / ₱315–₱1,015 (late registration) Where to Apply: Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 633-2487 / 0912-115-5000 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Building Permit
body: Building, Engineering & Zoning Building Permit Get a building permit from the Mapandan MEO. Simple: 3 days, Complex: 7 days, Highly Technical: 20 days per RA 11032. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Building Permit", "description": "A building permit is required under the National Building Code (PD 1096) and RA 11032. Processing times: Simple — 3 working days, Complex — 7 working days, Highly Technical — 20 working days. Includes site inspection, zoning and fire safety compliance.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Building, Engineering & Zoning", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description A building permit is a legal requirement under the National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096) for any construction, renovation, alteration, or demolition of a building or structure. The Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) of Mapandan reviews and issues building permits after ensuring compliance with safety standards, zoning, and structural requirements. Requirements Plans duly signed & sealed by licensed professionals Certified true copy of Tax Declaration (from Assessor Office) Xerox copy of land title (from Register of Deeds) Community Tax Certificate (from Treasury Office) Latest Tax receipts (from Treasury Office) Electrical & Sanitary permit (from Municipal Health Office) Confirmation of adjoining lot owners Certification from Barangay Captain Application for locational clearance (from Zoning Office) 2 Affidavits (from Notary Public) Affidavit of consent if not lot owner (from Notary Public) Fire Safety clearance (from BFP Office) Affidavit of adjoining lot owners Procedure Obtain a zoning clearance from the MPDC / Zoning Office. Prepare architectural and structural plans signed by licensed professionals. Submit all documents to the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) for review. Pay the building permit fees at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Receive the approved building permit after technical evaluation. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) Classification: Highly Technical Mode: in-person Processing Time: 3 working days (Simple) / 7 working days (Complex) / 20 working days (Highly Technical) per RA 11032 Fee: Based on project cost (schedule per National Building Code) Where to Apply: Municipal Engineering Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 636-9382 / 0918-962-7423 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Business Permit
body: Business Permitting & Licensing New Business Permit Apply for a new business permit at the BPLO in Mapandan. Includes endorsement to Engineering, MPDC, RHU, and BFP. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "New Business Permit", "description": "A business permit is required for all individuals or entities intending to operate a commercial business within the Municipality of Mapandan. This permit is issued after compliance with documentary and safety requirements and upon payment of applicable fees.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Business Permitting & Licensing", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description A business permit is required for all individuals or entities intending to operate a commercial business within the Municipality of Mapandan. This permit is issued after compliance with documentary and safety requirements and upon payment of applicable fees. Requirements Filled up UNIFIED Form / Community Tax Certificate (from BPLO/Treasury Office) DTI/SEC/CDA Registration (from DTI/SEC/CDA Office or Online Application) BIR COR, if available (from RDO Calasiao) Barangay Clearance (System Integrated) Procedure Fill up the UNIFIED form and submit necessary requirements for verification (10 min). BPLO encodes data into the e-BPLS System. BPLO endorses applicant to various offices: Engineering (Occupancy Certificate), MPDC (Zoning Certificate), RHU (Health Certificate & Sanitary Permit), BFP (Fire Safety Inspection Certificate) (44 min). Pay fees and charges at the Treasury Office. Proceed to the Mayor's Office for issuance of Business Permit. Claim business plate and sticker at the Treasury Office (10 min). Juridical — ₱500.00 + ₱2.00 for every ₱5,000 gross income (not to exceed ₱10,000). Interest of 24% per annum from March 1 to December 31.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Real Property & Revenue", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The Community Tax Certificate (cedula) is computed as follows: Individual — ₱5.00 basic + ₱1.00 for every ₱1,000 gross income from business, profession, or property, but in no case shall exceed ₱5,000.00. body: Real Property & Revenue Transfer of Land Ownership Transfer land ownership in Mapandan at the Assessor's Office. ₱150 recording fee, 30 minutes for Assessor processing. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Transfer of Land Ownership", "description": "Transfer of land ownership is the legal process of transferring property rights from one owner to another. This involves updating the Tax Declaration at the Assessor's Office. The transfer may be due to sale, donation, inheritance, or other legal means. Recording fee: ₱150.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Real Property & Revenue", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description Transfer of land ownership is the legal process of transferring property rights from one owner to another. The Municipal Assessor's Office (MASSO) records the transfer and updates the Tax Declaration under the new owner's name. The client first secures a tax clearance from the Treasury Office, then submits the transfer documents to the Assessor's Office. The Assessor records the transaction, cancels the old Tax Declaration, and issues a new one. Fee: ₱150 for recording. Requirements Deed of Sale, Deed of Donation, or other proof of transfer Tax Clearance from the Municipal Treasurer's Office Certified True Copy of Tax Declaration (from Assessor's Office) Valid Government-issued ID of the new owner BIR Certificate of Registration (if applicable) Procedure Secure a Tax Clearance from the Municipal Treasurer's Office. Obtain a Certified True Copy of the Tax Declaration from the Assessor's Office. Submit all required documents to the Assessor's Office. Assessor reviews and records the transfer (15 min). Assessor cancels the old Tax Declaration and prepares the new one (10 min). Pay ₱150 recording fee at the Treasury Office. Claim the new Tax Declaration under the new owner's name (5 min). Crutches, wheelchairs, and other devices available. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "PWD Assistive Devices", "description": "The MSWDO provides assistive devices such as crutches, wheelchairs, prosthesis, and other gadgets to Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) to help them integrate into the mainstream of community life.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Social Welfare — IDs & Certifications", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The MSWDO provides assistive devices such as crutches, wheelchairs, prosthesis, and other gadgets to Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) to help them integrate into the mainstream of community life. body: Social Welfare — IDs & Certifications OSCA Death Aid Benefits Claim OSCA Death Aid Benefits for deceased senior citizens. Learn about requirements and the claims process at the MSWDO. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "OSCA Death Aid Benefits", "description": "The OSCA Death Aid Benefits provide financial assistance to families of deceased Senior Citizens. body: Social Assistance & Protection Disaster Relief Assistance Disaster relief assistance for families affected by calamities in Mapandan. Relief goods and housing repair assistance available. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Disaster Relief Assistance", "description": "The MSWDO provides disaster relief assistance and rehabilitation services to families affected by floods, typhoons, fires, and other calamities. The service includes distribution of relief goods and financial assistance for housing repair.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Social Assistance & Protection", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The MSWDO provides disaster relief assistance and rehabilitation services to families affected by floods, typhoons, fires, and other calamities. The MSWDO coordinates with the LGU, PSWDO, and DSWD Field Office I. Requirements Master list of affected families (from Barangay Captain) Barangay certificate Certificate of Indigency Procedure Report to the Barangay Captain the extent of damage. MSWDO receives list of affected families and endorses to concerned social worker. Verification and inspection team (with Engineering, PNP, DSWD) assesses the damage. For totally destroyed houses, MSWDO prepares project proposal for ESA funding. Financial assistance (ESA) is distributed to qualified beneficiaries. MSWDO monitors and evaluates project implementation for house repair/reconstruction. title: Pre Natal
body: Health Services Pre-Natal Consultation Free pre-natal consultation for antenatal women at the Mapandan Rural Health Unit. Lab tests and health teaching included. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Pre-Natal Consultation", "description": "The RHU provides pre-natal consultation services for antenatal women. The service includes registration, physical examination, laboratory tests, health teaching, and classification of pregnancy risk level.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Health Services", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The RHU provides pre-natal consultation services for antenatal women. The service includes registration in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR), OB history, vital signs, Leopold's maneuver, fetal heartbeat assessment, and fundic height measurement. Routine laboratory tests (CBC, urinalysis, HBsAg, RPR) are requested. The MHO conducts complete physical examination, interprets laboratory results, and provides health teaching on proper nutrition, prenatal care, breastfeeding, and immunization. High-risk patients are referred to higher-level facilities. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Medical Records, Laboratory Results, Prescription for Medicines (from previous physician, if any) Procedure Register in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR). Midwife encodes OB history, vital signs, and performs Leopold's maneuver. Request for routine laboratory tests (CBC, urinalysis, HBsAg Screening, RPR test). MHO performs complete physical examination and interprets laboratory results. If high-risk, patient is referred to a higher level of facility. Health teaching on proper nutrition, prenatal care, breastfeeding, and immunization. Service Details Responsible Office: Rural Health Unit (RHU) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 55 minutes per client Fee: Free Where to Apply: Rural Health Unit, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1874 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Family Planning
body: Health Services Family Planning Free family planning services at the Mapandan RHU. Counselling and provision of oral pills and injectables for couples. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Family Planning", "description": "The RHU provides family planning services to couples, including counselling on different methods, assessment of suitability, and provision of oral pills and DMPA injectables.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Health Services", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The RHU provides family planning services to couples, including counselling on different family planning methods along with their advantages and disadvantages. The MHO assesses whether the chosen method is suitable and appropriate for the mother. Available methods include oral pills and DMPA injectables. Data encoding, obstetric history, and vital signs are recorded during the consultation. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Procedure Register in the log book. Midwife encodes data, obstetric history, and vital signs. title: Tb Dots
body: Health Services TB DOTS Treatment Free TB DOTS treatment at the Mapandan RHU. Sputum testing, GeneXpert, and anti-TB medication available. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "TB DOTS Treatment", "description": "The RHU provides Directly Observed Treatment Short Course (TB DOTS) for patients with tuberculosis. The service includes sputum examination, GeneXpert testing, physical examination, and provision of anti-TB drugs.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Health Services", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The RHU provides Directly Observed Treatment Short Course (TB DOTS) for patients with tuberculosis. The service includes registration, sputum examination, GeneXpert/TBDC testing, physical examination, and provision of anti-TB drugs with proper intake instructions. The MHO maintains patient confidentiality and monitors treatment compliance. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Medical Records, Prescription of Medicines (from previous physician, if any) Chest X-Ray PA Result (from government or private diagnostic facility) Procedure Register in the log book. Consent is secured and confidentiality is maintained. MHO conducts physical examination of patient. Anti-TB drugs are given with record and patient is advised on proper intake. title: Laboratory
body: Health Services Laboratory Examination Laboratory services at the Mapandan RHU. CBC, urinalysis, fecalysis, pregnancy test, and more available at affordable rates. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Laboratory Examination", "description": "The RHU primary laboratory provides various diagnostic tests including ABO/RH typing, pregnancy test, CBC, urinalysis, fecalysis, Hepatitis B screening, and fasting blood sugar (FBS).", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Health Services", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The RHU primary laboratory provides various diagnostic tests including ABO/RH typing, pregnancy test, CBC, urinalysis, fecalysis, Hepatitis B screening, and fasting blood sugar (FBS). The MHO provides a laboratory request, and the Medical Technologist conducts the examination. Results are interpreted by the MHO who prescribes medications as needed. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Physician's laboratory request / referral Procedure Register in the log book. Midwife encodes data, vital signs, and asks about symptoms. MHO conducts physical examination and requests laboratory tests. Submit specimen for testing. Available tests: ABO/RH typing (₱100), Pregnancy test (₱50), CBC (₱150), Urinalysis (₱65), Fecalysis (₱65), Hepatitis B screening (₱200), FBS (₱100). Medical Technologist conducts the laboratory examination. MHO interprets laboratory results and prescribes medications. Service Details Responsible Office: Rural Health Unit (RHU) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: ~2 hours per client (varies by tests requested) Fee: Varies by test (₱50–₱200) Where to Apply: Rural Health Unit Primary Laboratory, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1874 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Nutrition Immunization
body: Health Services Nutrition & Immunization Program Free nutrition and immunization programs for children at the Mapandan RHU. Malnourishment intervention and NIP vaccines available. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Nutrition & Immunization Program", "description": "The RHU implements the Nutrition Program for malnourished children (0–59 months and older) and the National Immunization Program (NIP) for children against vaccine-preventable diseases.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Health Services", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The RHU implements the Nutrition Program for malnourished children (0–59 months and older) and the National Immunization Program (NIP) for children against vaccine-preventable diseases. The nutrition program includes assessment, deworming, feeding with nutrient-dense food, and monthly monitoring. The immunization program administers age-appropriate vaccines after reviewing the child's records and checking vital signs. Requirements Birth Certificate (Municipal Civil Registry) Medical Records, Vaccination Records (from hospital of birth or pediatrician) Procedure For malnourished children (0–59 months): Barangay Nutrition Scholar assesses weight and height. Physician refers to RHU for deworming and medical intervention. Child is fed with nutrient-dense food (high carbohydrate and protein). Monthly monitoring of weight, height, and alertness. For immunization: BHW interviews child's information and reviews records. Midwife checks vital signs (weight and temperature). Midwife administers age-appropriate vaccine. Midwife advises parent on child care and expected outcome. Schedule next vaccination. Service Details Responsible Office: Rural Health Unit (RHU) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 50 minutes per client Fee: Free Where to Apply: Rural Health Unit, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1874 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Electrical Zoning
body: Zoning & Planning Electrical Zoning Clearance Get an electrical zoning clearance from the MPDC in Mapandan. Required before obtaining an electrical permit. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Electrical Zoning Clearance", "description": "A zoning clearance is required for electrical permits. The MPDC/Zoning Office evaluates the application, conducts land use assessment, and issues the Zoning Compliance Certificate for electrical installations.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Zoning & Planning", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description A zoning clearance is required for electrical permits. The MPDC/Zoning Office evaluates the application, conducts land use assessment, and issues the Zoning Compliance Certificate for electrical installations. The process includes site evaluation/inspection, computation of fees, and approval by the Zoning Officer. Requirements Application for Zoning Permit (from MPDC) Accomplished Individual Assessment for Application of Temporary Housing Unit Form Tax Declaration of lot (from Assessor Office) Current Tax receipts (from Treasury Office) Affidavit of consent of lot owner Site development sketch indicating the ROW Affidavit of consent for Right of Way (from lot owner) Certification from Barangay Captain Procedure Inquire at the MPDC office and secure the application form. MPDC staff conducts interview and provides forms. Accomplish forms and prepare all required documents. MPDC checks and evaluates forms and required documents. Request for site evaluation/inspection. Land use assessment conducted. Go to Zoning office for computation of fees and charges. Pay fees at the Treasury Office. Present receipts to MPDC. Submit one photocopy of all forms and documents. MPDC prepares and submits documents. Zoning Officer approves application. Client signs logbook. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Planning and Development Office (MPDC) / Zoning Office Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: ~1.5 hours Fee: ₱330 (Zoning fee ₱200 + Affidavit ₱100 + Documentary Stamp ₱30) Where to Apply: MPDC / Zoning Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: 0933-865-9150 / 0925-708-8808 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Business Zoning
body: Zoning & Planning Business Zoning Clearance Get a business zoning clearance from the MPDC in Mapandan. Required before applying for a business permit. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Business Zoning Clearance", "description": "A zoning clearance is required for all businesses applying for a business permit. The MPDC/Zoning Office encodes the business, conducts geotagging, computes fees, and issues the Business Zoning Clearance.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Zoning & Planning", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description A zoning clearance is required for all businesses applying for a business permit. The MPDC/Zoning Office encodes the business to the DTI-Local Data Capture Sheet, conducts geotagging of the business establishment, computes fees in the iBPLS web application, and issues the Business Zoning Clearance. The process is part of the integrated business permit system. Requirements Unified Application Form for Business Permit (from BPLO) Procedure Go to MPDC / Zoning Office for zoning endorsement. MPDC encodes business to DTI-Local Data Capture Sheet Annex B. Geotagging of business establishment is conducted. Computation of fees in the iBPLS web application: Zoning fee (New Business ₱720, Renewal varies) + Inspection fee (₱100). MPDC prepares and issues Business Zoning Clearance. Complete endorsement is recorded. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Planning and Development Office (MPDC) / Zoning Office Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: ~24 minutes Fee: ₱820 (Zoning fee ₱720 + Inspection fee ₱100) Where to Apply: MPDC / Zoning Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: 0933-865-9150 / 0925-708-8808 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Financial Claims Payment
body: Real Property & Revenue Financial Assistance Claims Payment Claim financial assistance payments at the Mapandan Treasury Office. Cash for ≤₱3,000, check for >₱3,000. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Financial Assistance Claims Payment", "description": "Payment of financial assistance and other claims for indigent residents. The Treasury Office verifies documents and releases cash (≤₱3,000) or check (>₱3,000).", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Real Property & Revenue", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description Payment of financial assistance and other claims for indigent residents of Mapandan. The Treasury Office verifies documents, checks signatures, and releases payment. Cash is released for amounts ₱3,000 and below; checks are issued for amounts exceeding ₱3,000. An authorization letter is required if a representative claims on behalf of the beneficiary. title: Seed Certification
body: Agriculture Seed Certification Services Get seed certification services from the Mapandan MAO. Free lab analysis and seed tags for registered seed growers. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Seed Certification Services", "description": "The Municipal Agriculturist provides technical and extension services for seed certification, including seed sampling, laboratory analysis, and issuance of seed tags for registered seed growers.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Agriculture", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The Municipal Agriculturist provides technical and extension services for seed certification. The service includes seed sampling in the presence of the Seed Inspector, laboratory analysis, and issuance of seed tags. Available to registered members of the Seed Grower Association. The Municipal Agriculturist coordinates with the Seeds Laboratory for analysis. Requirements Membership in Seed Grower Association Actual harvest date notification to Seeds Inspector Procedure Submit/show requirements and inform the Seeds Inspector of the actual date of harvest. Municipal Agriculturist confirms presence at the date of harvest (10 min). Gather seed samples in the presence of the Seed Inspector and submit to the seed laboratory for analysis (10 min). Seeds Laboratory analyzes seed samples, tags, and prepares report (15 min). Receive result of the seed analysis and sign log book. Seeds Inspector delivers seed tags and discusses results (15 min). Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Agriculturist Office (MAO) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: ~50 minutes Fee: Free Where to Apply: Municipal Agriculture Office, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1873 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Crop Protection
body: Agriculture Crop Protection Technical Services Free crop protection services from the Mapandan MAO. Farm inspection, plant analysis, and pest management recommendations. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Crop Protection Technical Services", "description": "The Municipal Agriculturist provides technical and extension services for crop protection, including farm inspection, plant analysis, and recommendations for pest and disease management.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Agriculture", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The Municipal Agriculturist provides technical and extension services for crop protection. The Agricultural Technologist conducts farm inspections, examines plant health, submits samples to DA-RCPC for analysis, and provides recommendations for pest and disease management. Available to registered farmers. Requirements Registration as a farmer Notification of farm visit schedule to assigned Agricultural Technologist Procedure Inform the assigned Agricultural Technologist of the actual date of farm visit for crop protection. title: Demolition Permit
body: Building, Engineering & Zoning Demolition Permit Get a demolition permit from the Mapandan Municipal Engineer. Required before demolishing any building or structure. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Demolition Permit", "description": "A demolition permit is required before any demolition of a building or structure. The Municipal Engineer conducts initial assessment, site inspection, and issues the permit after fee computation.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Building, Engineering & Zoning", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description A demolition permit is required before any demolition of a building or structure in Mapandan. The Municipal Engineer conducts initial assessment of the application, site inspection, and computation of fees. The permit is issued after payment and verification of all requirements. Requirements Application for demolition permit Approved demolition plans (if applicable) Proof of ownership or authorization from owner Procedure Report to the Engineering Office for assessment of your application (15 min). title: Electrical Permit
body: Building, Engineering & Zoning Electrical Permit Get an electrical permit from the Mapandan Municipal Engineer. Required for all electrical installations and wiring. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Electrical Permit", "description": "An electrical permit is required for electrical installations and wiring. The Municipal Engineer evaluates the application, conducts site inspection, and issues the permit after zoning and fire safety compliance.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Building, Engineering & Zoning", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description An electrical permit is required for electrical installations and wiring within Mapandan. The Municipal Engineer evaluates the application, conducts site inspection, computes fees based on total connected loads, and endorses to the Zoning Officer and BFP for compliance. The permit is issued after all clearances are obtained. Requirements Confirmation of adjoining lot owners Barangay Clearance Certified true copy of Tax Declaration Xerox copy of land title (if any) Latest tax payment Community Tax Certificate Signed & sealed form of electrical permits Application for zoning clearance Affidavits Procedure Report to Engineering Office for assessment. Staff provides necessary forms (15 min). Fill up electrical permit forms and submit to the Building Official. Staff evaluates requirements and conducts site inspection (30 min + 1 hour). Staff computes assessment fee and endorses to Zoning Officer & BFP (15 min + 15 min). Pay fees at Treasury Office. Zoning officer & Fire Dept conduct inspection (10 min). Receive Zoning/Locational & Fire Safety clearance (15 min). Receive the Electrical Permit (2 min). Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Engineer's Office Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: ~2 hours Fee: Varies based on total connected loads Where to Apply: Municipal Engineer's Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 636-9382 / 0918-962-7423 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Birth Registration
body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Birth Registration Register a birth at the Mapandan MCR. Standard fee ₱115, late registration ₱315–₱1,015. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Birth Registration", "description": "Registration of birth with the Municipal Civil Registrar. Covers registration by attending midwife/hilot, unmarried parents, hospital administrators, and late registration with PSA verification.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Civil Registry & Vital Records", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description Registration of birth at the Municipal Civil Registrar. Covers three pathways: (1) Attending midwife/hilot reports child's birth — requires Marriage Certificate of parents and Mun. Form 102; (2) Unmarried parents — requires Community Tax Certificate; (3) Hospital administrator — requires Accomplished Mun. Form 102. Late registration requires negative PSA certification and supporting documents. Fees: Misc Fee ₱115 (standard), ₱215 (unmarried), ₱100 (hospital), ₱315–₱1,015 (late registration depending on age). Requirements Marriage Certificate of parents from PSA (for attending midwife/hilot registration) Community Tax Certificate from Treasury Office (for unmarried parents) Accomplished Mun. Form 102 from MCR (for hospital registration) Negative certification from PSA (for late registration) Affidavit of delayed registration (for late registration) Supporting evidence: Baptismal Certificate, School records, ITR, Insurance Policy, Medical records, Barangay certification (for late registration) Procedure Attending midwife/hilot reports child's birth. MCR evaluates information and registers (10 min). For unmarried parents: Hospital admin or representative prepares documents (15 min). For late registration: Apply at MCR, verify from CRIS/Registry Book. If negative, submit requirements. Data typed in Certificate of Live Birth (15 min typing). MCR approves registration (after 10 days of posting for late registration). Secure copy of birth certificate. MCR releases documents (3 min). Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 10 minutes (standard) to 10 days (late registration posting) Fee: ₱115 (standard) / ₱215 (unmarried) / ₱100 (hospital) / ₱315–₱1,015 (late registration) Where to Apply: Municipal Civil Registrar's Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 633-2487 / 0912-115-5000 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Legal Document Registration
body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Legal Document Registration Register legal documents at the Mapandan MCR. Legitimation, acknowledgement, and RA 9255 services available. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Legal Document Registration", "description": "Registration of legal documents including Affidavit of Legitimation, Affidavit of Acknowledgement, and RA 9255 (use of father's surname). Fee: ₱215–₱315.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Civil Registry & Vital Records", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description Registration of legal documents at the Municipal Civil Registrar. Covers Affidavit of Legitimation (for parents not married before child's birth), Affidavit of Acknowledgement (for fathers acknowledging children), and RA 9255 applications (use of father's surname). Fee: ₱315 for legitimation, ₱215 for acknowledgement and RA 9255. MCR examines documents, prepares attachments, and makes annotations on the registry book. Requirements Affidavit of Legitimation (for legitimation) CENOMAR from PSA Certified copy of child's COLB from MCR Certified copy of parent's Marriage Certificate from MCR Affidavit of Acknowledgement (for acknowledgement) Affidavit to use the surname of the father (for RA 9255) Other supporting documents: baptismal certificate, insurance policies Procedure For legitimation: Parents not married before child's birth submit requirements. MCR examines documents, prepares attachments, and annotates registry book (₱315, 20–25 min). For acknowledgement: Father acknowledges children. Same procedure as above (₱215, 20–25 min). For RA 9255: Parents apply to use father's surname. Same procedure (₱215, 20–25 min). MCR annotates and approves documents (5 min). body: Sangguniang Bayan Legislative Documents A comprehensive database of municipal ordinances, resolutions, executive issuances, and fiscal data — tracing Mapandan's legislative record from its 1887 founding to the present. Categories Hide menu < Governance framework 5 Legal Basis Historical Origins Ordinances Resolutions Executive issuances Fiscal 14 Ordinance Categories Revenue vs Expenditure Budget Growth Trends 4 Legislative process 9 Ordinance vs resolution 2 Ordinance Resolution Governance framework Ordinances Resolutions Executive issuances Fiscal Trends Legislative process Ordinance vs resolution Framework Local governance & statutory origins Legal Basis The Municipality of Mapandan operates under Republic Act No. 7160 (Local Government Code of 1991), situated within the Third Congressional District of Pangasinan. The Sangguniang Bayan — a unicameral local legislative council — exercises municipal legislative power, presided by the Municipal Vice Mayor and composed of elected councilors alongside ex-officio representatives from the Liga ng mga Barangay and the Sangguniang Kabataan Federation. Historical Origins Originally an agricultural barrio of Mangaldan referred to as balon baley ("new town"), Mapandan was first established as an independent pueblo pursuant to Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, promulgated by Governor General Emilio Bravo on December 28, 1887. Following population and fiscal losses caused by an epidemic in 1905 that temporarily reverted Mapandan to Mangaldan's jurisdiction, the municipality was re-established under American civil administration through Executive Order No. 10, signed by Governor General James F. Smith in 1909.
