No. 5, S-2024 Pipeline Legislative pipeline The legislative pipeline under the Local Government Code of 1991. 1 Filing A proposed ordinance is filed with the Sangguniang Bayan for consideration. 2 First Reading Initial reading and referral to the relevant committee for review. 3 Committee Hearing The committee holds hearings and deliberates on the proposal. 4 Committee Report Findings and recommendations are submitted back to the full council. 5 Second Reading Detailed floor discussion and debate on the proposed ordinance. 6 Third & Final Reading Final vote by the Sangguniang Bayan. 7 Mayor's Approval The Municipal Mayor reviews and approves the enacted ordinance. 8 Provincial Review Submitted to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Pangasinan for legal review under Sections 56 and 57 of R.A. 7160. 9 Posting & Effect The approved ordinance is posted publicly and takes effect across all 15 constituent barangays. Key Distinction Ordinance vs. Resolution Under the Local Government Code of 1991, the Sangguniang Bayan enacts two types of legislative measures: Ordinance A legislative measure that enacts a permanent rule or policy . Ordinances carry the force of law, create offices, levy taxes, or regulate conduct. They require three readings, publication, and the Mayor's approval (or passage by 2/3 override of a veto). Resolution A legislative measure that expresses the sentiment, intent, or opinion of the Sangguniang Bayan on a specific matter. Resolutions are used for internal housekeeping, requesting national action, or authorizing one-time transactions. They require only one reading and are not subject to publication.

body: Tungkol sa Better Mapandan About Better Mapandan An independent civic transparency portal for the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "AboutPage", "name": "About Better Mapandan", "url": "https://bettermapandan.org/about/", "description": "Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities.", "mainEntity": { "@type": "WebSite", "name": "Better Mapandan", "url": "https://bettermapandan.org" } } About Mapandan So baley Kasaysayan Mapandan was created as an independent pueblo on December 28, 1887, through Director General No. 39. After a period of financial insolvency (1905–1908) when it was re-absorbed into Mangaldan, the town was re-established as an independent municipality in 1909 under Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. The town was named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants in the area. Heograpiya Mapandan is a third-class municipality in the province of Pangasinan, Philippines. It covers a land area of 32.92 km² and is composed of 15 barangays. The municipality is located in the western part of Pangasinan, bordered by the Lingayen Gulf to the north and the Agno River floodplain to the south. Population 38,228 PSA Census 2024 Land Area 32.92 km² MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Saray barangay 15 DILG / Comelec Cultural Heritage Local traditions and community life Pandan Festival Held annually during the second week of April, the Pandan Festival celebrates Mapandan's cultural heritage with street dancing, pageants, and community gatherings. Pandan Festival Town Plaza The historic center of Mapandan's community life and civic gatherings. Town Plaza Agriculture Rice fields and farmland across Mapandan's countryside — the agricultural heart of the municipality. Agriculture Kasaysayan Mapandan diad saray taon 1887–1909 Pagtatakda tan Unang Pamamahala From southern barrios of Mangaldan to an independent pueblo—and back again. Mapandan’s first two decades were defined by the courage of its founders, the fragility of a new town, and the determination to rise again. Basaen pa Before 1887: Southern barrios of Mangaldan Before Mapandan existed as an independent pueblo, the area belonged to Mangaldan. The future municipality consisted of southern communities including Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac. The movement toward establishing a separate town was initiated by ten local leaders: Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, Andres Bongato, Ambrosio Calimlim, Valeriano Tamondong, Tomas Aquino, Fulgencio Nato, Filomeno Sarmiento, Jose Lalas, and Florencio Datuin. December 28, 1887: Mapandan becomes a pueblo Mapandan was established as an independent pueblo through Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, signed by Governor General Emilio Bravo. The new pueblo was initially composed of the southern barrios of Mangaldan: Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac. The first town center: Torres The first center of the new pueblo was in what is now Barangay Torres. The area had abundant pandan plants and was associated with a church where Fr. Jose Torres served as parish priest. However, the location proved inconvenient—too close to the southern boundary and too far from communities to the north. The center was eventually transferred to an area that had previously been a sitio of Apaya. Much of the land in the new Poblacion was owned by the Aquino family. Leon Hilario Aquino encouraged settlement by subdividing land into uniform lots and making them available to families. 1903: The epidemic An epidemic severely affected Mapandan, causing major population depletion, residents leaving the town, declining municipal resources, and a financial crisis. The 1903 census recorded Mapandan’s population at 4,198. 1905–1908: Return to Mangaldan Because of the population and financial problems caused by the epidemic, Mapandan was temporarily returned to its mother municipality, Mangaldan. 1909: Restoration Mapandan was formally re-established as a municipality under Executive Order No. 10, signed by Governor General James F. Smith. 1910s–1940s Paglago na Agrikultura tan Panahon na Gubat After its restoration, Mapandan developed as a predominantly agricultural community. Farming remained central to the local economy, with rice becoming the municipality’s principal crop. The decades ahead would bring war, occupation, and the beginning of reconstruction. Basaen pa Agricultural foundations Rice became the municipality’s principal crop and livestock raising developed as an important secondary livelihood. The municipality’s current seal still reflects these agricultural foundations through its rice, cattle, chicken and hog imagery. 1940s: War, occupation and rebuilding The Second World War interrupted the development of communities across Pangasinan. In the postwar years, Mapandan’s communities entered a period of reconstruction and social and economic change. The decades following the war also brought changes in landholding, agriculture, education and local community organization. 1940s–1970s Pagpapaunlad na Komunidad Kalpasan na Gubat After the war, Mapandan’s communities began to take shape. New barangays were formed, land ownership changed hands, and the municipality entered a period of organized community development. Basaen pa Barangays begin taking shape Instead of only telling municipal history, the history of how Mapandan’s communities formed tells an equally important story. Sta. Maria — Formerly part of Luyan, developed from former hacienda land. Tenants gained opportunities to own the land they had been farming after the war. It became a separate barrio in 1965. Golden — Formerly Amanoaoac North, a sitio of Amanoaoac. Its name was associated with the Golden Distillery, which operated after liberation. Golden became a separate barangay in 1967. Torres — The first seat of Mapandan, which once contained several sitios that later developed into separate barangays. 1967–1973: Community development Golden was officially approved as a separate barangay in 1967. The community then underwent substantial development including road improvement, waterworks, school construction, sports facilities, cooperative organization, agricultural training, and sanitation programs. 1972 — Golden was recognized as a SEATO/PACD Model Village, receiving a national-level award presented in Malacañang on September 8, 1972. 1972–1973 — Coral became a barangay through Municipal Council Resolution No. 87 (May 4, 1972), Provincial Board Resolution No. 155 (August 10, 1972), and Proclamation No. 11 (April 25, 1973), followed by a special election for barangay officials on May 6, 1973. 1980s–2001 Modernization Mapandan’s population grew substantially, its services expanded, and infrastructure developed. The municipality moved from historical survival toward economic growth. Read more Population growth Mapandan’s population grew steadily through the second half of the 20th century: 20,094 in 1980, 25,622 in 1990, and 30,775 in 2000. Infrastructure and services The municipality expanded roads, schools, health facilities, and public services. Community organizations grew alongside the population. 2002–2024 Pagpapaunlad ed Ika-21 Siglo From a new municipal classification to healthcare expansion and digital government—Mapandan enters the 21st century with growing services, cultural pride, and a more connected community. Read more 2002: A new municipal classification Mapandan was elevated to a third-class municipality. The municipality credits then-Mayor Jose Ferdinand Z. Calimlim Jr. with spearheading income and revenue-generation strategies that contributed to the municipality’s elevation. 2010s: Celebrating the Pandan heritage The Pandan Festival developed into an important annual celebration of Mapandan’s identity, culture and community. The 9th Pandan Festival was held alongside the town fiesta from March 11–19, 2018. 2017–2018: Early digital government efforts The municipal government began developing an online presence that made government information, public notices, disaster information and community announcements accessible through the web. 2022–2024: Expanding healthcare access National health infrastructure funding supported the development of the Mapandan Super Health Center. The 2022 General Appropriations Act included ₱6.5 million for the project. Its first phase was inaugurated on March 15, 2024, expanding access to laboratory, dental and primary healthcare services for residents of Mapandan and nearby communities. 2020s: Government services go digital Mapandan’s government information infrastructure increasingly incorporates digital channels, including information and access guidance for the national eGovPH platform. 2024: Mapandan today More than 130 years after its establishment as a pueblo, Mapandan is a 15-barangay municipality with a population of 38,228. Its history has been shaped by migration, agriculture, community organization, local government, cultural traditions and continuing investment in public services. ← 1 / 5 → Source: Mayor Karl Vega, “History of Mapandan” — YouTube Sources & Historical Notes Historical accounts drawn from municipal archives, provincial records, and published heritage studies of Pangasinan. Municipality of Mapandan — Municipal Profile Municipality of Mapandan — Physical Characteristics Philippine Statistics Authority — Mapandan PSGC Philippine News Agency — Super Health Center Inauguration Paglago na Populasyon Mapandan diad census Populasyon base ed taon na census Year Population 1903 4,198 1918 6,049 1939 7,286 1948 9,836 1960 13,065 1970 16,653 1980 20,094 1990 25,622 2000 30,775 2010 34,439 2020 38,058 2024 38,228 Source: Philippine Statistics Authority, Census of Population (1903–2024) About the Project Anto so Better Mapandan? Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities. Say Misyon Mi To make government information accessible, understandable, and actionable for every Mapandan resident. We believe that open data strengthens democracy and empowers communities to participate meaningfully in local governance. Panon to Mantrabaho We compile publicly available government data — from COA audit reports, PSA census data, municipal disclosures, and provincial issuances — into a single, easy-to-navigate website. Every piece of information is sourced and attributed. Open Source The source code is publicly available. Developers can contribute, audit, and improve the platform. View on GitHub → Independent Say Better Mapandan et independent civic transparency portal. Aliwa iya opisyal a website na gobierno tan aliwa iya kaabay, inendorso, odino pinatatakbo na Municipality of Mapandan odino arum a ahensya na gobierno. Pinapakewilian na Volunteers Built and maintained entirely by volunteers. No government funding is used. Cost to the people of Mapandan: ₱0. Contribute Makisali Better Mapandan thrives on community participation. Here's how you can help: I-ulat so Aliwan a Tama a Impormasyon Spotted an error? Help us keep the data accurate by reporting mistakes. Report an error → Mang-contribute na Code Developers can contribute features, fix bugs, or improve accessibility on GitHub. Fork on GitHub → I-verify so Datos Help verify government information by cross-referencing with official sources. Submit verification → I-share ed Saray Residente Spread the word about Better Mapandan so more residents can access government information. Disclaimer Mahalagang Abiso Say Better Mapandan et independent civic transparency portal. Information presented on this site is compiled from publicly available government sources and community research. While we strive for accuracy, we cannot guarantee the completeness or timeliness of all data. For official government information, please visit mapandan.gov.ph or contact the municipal government directly.

title: Pahayag ed Aksesibilidad — BetterMapandan.org
description: Panag-ikagapos tan saray pamantayan ed aksesibilidad para ed Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Suporta Accessibility Statement Sikayo so compromiso mi pian nayarin a maakses na amin a residente so impormasyon na gobierno. Our commitment Better Mapandan is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We continually improve the user experience for everyone and apply the relevant accessibility standards. Conformance Status We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at the AA level. These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible for people with disabilities. Measures Taken We have implemented the following accessibility features across the site: Semantic HTML structure Skip-to-content navigation link Visible focus indicators Sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 minimum) Keyboard-accessible navigation Screen-reader-friendly labels Descriptive link text Proper heading hierarchy Accessibility features Keyboard Navigation All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard. Use Tab to move between elements, Enter to activate links and buttons, and Escape to close overlays. Screen Readers The site uses semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and proper heading hierarchy to ensure screen readers can navigate the content effectively. Color & Contrast All text meets WCAG AA contrast requirements. Information is never conveyed through color alone — icons, labels, and text are always provided alongside color coding. Text Resizing The site uses relative units (rem, em) for text sizing. Users can resize text up to 200% without loss of content or functionality. Forms All form inputs are associated with labels. Error messages are descriptive and programmatically associated with the relevant input fields. Tables Data tables include proper header associations ( <th scope> ), captions where appropriate, and are responsive on mobile devices. Known limitations We are aware of the following accessibility limitations and are working to address them: PDF documents: Some linked government documents (COA reports, provincial issuances) may not be fully accessible. We provide HTML summaries where possible. Interactive maps: The Leaflet map is navigable via keyboard but may present challenges for screen reader users. We provide alternative text descriptions and a data table fallback. Third-party content: Embedded content from external government websites may not meet the same accessibility standards. Feedback We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of Better Mapandan. If you encounter accessibility barriers, please let us know: Report an Issue Use our reporting form to describe the accessibility issue, the page URL, and your browser/device information. Report accessibility issue → GitHub Issues Developers can file accessibility issues directly on our GitHub repository. Open GitHub issue →

No. Say Better Mapandan et independent civic transparency portal. Aliwa iya opisyal a website na gobierno tan aliwa iya kaabay, inendorso, odino pinatatakbo na Municipality of Mapandan odino arum a ahensya na gobierno. For official information, visit mapandan.gov.ph . How is this project funded? Better Mapandan is entirely volunteer-run and uses no government funding. The cost to the people of Mapandan is ₱0. Hosting and domain costs are covered by the BetterGov.ph initiative. Where does the data come from? All data is compiled from publicly available government sources: COA audit reports, PSA census data, DILG Full Disclosure filings , BLGF treasury data, provincial issuances, and municipal announcements. Every source is attributed on the page where the data appears. How do I report incorrect information? Visit our Report Incorrect Information page. Provide the page URL, the specific error, and the correct information if known. Our volunteers will review and update the data. Services Government services How do I get a birth certificate? Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) at the 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion. Bring a valid ID and the required fee. Processing time is typically 3–5 working days. See the full requirements on the Birth Certificate service page . How do I apply for a business permit? Visit the Municipal Treasurer's Office (MTO) with your DTI/SEC registration, barangay clearance, and other required documents. New permits are processed in 3–5 working days. See the Business Permit service page for full details. How do I get a building permit? Apply through the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO). Building permits require a zoning clearance, architectural plans, and structural plans. Processing takes 10–15 working days. See the Building Permit service page . How do I request a barangay clearance? Visit your barangay hall with a valid ID. Barangay clearances are typically issued the same day. This is often a prerequisite for other government transactions. Data & Transparency Data questions What does "Placeholder" mean on data? Some data is marked as "Placeholder" when the exact figure is not yet available from official sources. We use reasonable estimates based on available data and clearly mark these so residents know the difference between verified and estimated figures. How often is the data updated? Each data section includes a "Last updated" timestamp. Major updates happen when new COA audit reports, PSA census data, or municipal financial disclosures become available. The site is continuously improved by volunteers. Can I download the data? Yes. The Statistics page includes CSV download options for chart data. The Transparency page provides links to source documents. All data is publicly available and free to reuse under open data principles. How can I verify the data myself? Every data section includes a source attribution and, where available, a link to the original document. You can cross-reference with official sources like the COA website, PSA, or the municipal government directly. Contact Still have questions? For government services Contact the relevant office directly. See the Government Directory for phone numbers and email addresses. For this website Report issues, suggest improvements, or contribute on GitHub . For data corrections, use the Report Incorrect Information form.

title: Privacy Policy — BetterMapandan.org
description: Privacy policy para ed Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Legal Privacy Policy Panon mi a mangasiwa ed datos diad Better Mapandan civic transparency portal. Overview Say Better Mapandan et independent civic transparency portal. Aliwa iya opisyal a website na gobierno tan aliwa iya kaabay, inendorso, odino pinatatakbo na Municipality of Mapandan odino arum a ahensya na gobierno. We collect minimal data and are committed to protecting your privacy. Information We Collect Automatically collected: When you visit Better Mapandan, our hosting provider (GitHub Pages) may collect standard web server logs including your IP address, browser type, referring URL, and pages visited. This is standard server operation and is not used to identify individual visitors. Search queries: The search functionality runs entirely in your browser. Your search queries are never sent to a server or stored. Language preference: If you use the language switcher (when available), your preference is stored locally in your browser and is never transmitted to us. How We Use Information We do not use, sell, or share personal information. Server logs are used only for maintaining the website and understanding usage patterns in aggregate. Cookies Better Mapandan does not use cookies. The language preference is stored using localStorage , which is a browser-only storage mechanism and is not transmitted to any server. Third-Party Services The site loads the following external resources: Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) — for font loading Open-Meteo API (open-meteo.com) — for weather data (loaded only on the homepage) Leaflet / OpenStreetMap — for the interactive map (loaded only on the homepage) These services have their own privacy policies. We do not share any personal data with them. Data Sources All government data presented on this site is compiled from publicly available official sources. This data is already public and is presented here for informational purposes. Changes to This Policy This privacy policy may be updated from time to time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date. Contact For privacy-related inquiries, please open an issue on our GitHub repository or use the report form .

Split: 30% Quick Response Fund (emergency relief) + 70% pre-disaster preparedness and mitigation. Statutory Special Education Fund (SEF) Financed through a 1% tax levy on assessed real property values under Section 235 of R.A. 7160. Co-administered by the Municipal School Board. Restricted to supplementary funding for public schools: facility construction, educational materials, instructional support, and sports development. Statutory Limitasyon na Personnel Services Section 325(a) of R.A. 7160 limits total personnel spending to 45% or 55% of total annual regular income depending on LGU classification. title: Agriculture Subsidy
body: Agriculture Agricultural Subsidies Apply for agricultural subsidies in Mapandan. Seeds at 50% discount, plus technical assistance and livestock services. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Agricultural Subsidies", "description": "The Municipal Agriculture Office provides subsidized agricultural programs including seeds (hybrid and inbred at 50% DA-RFU subsidy), fertilizers, farm equipment, and technical assistance. Also provides seed certification, crop protection services, and animal anti-rabies vaccination.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Agriculture", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon The Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) provides various government-subsidized agricultural programs to support local farmers and fisherfolk in Mapandan. These programs include subsidies for seeds, fertilizers, farm equipment, and technical assistance to improve agricultural productivity and livelihood. Availability of subsidies depends on national and provincial funding allocations. Saray Kinakailangan Farmer registration with the Municipal Agriculture Office Barangay certification of residency and farming activity Farm location and land area information Proseso Register with the Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) as a farmer or fisherfolk. Secure a barangay certification confirming your farming activity and residency. Submit your registration and requirements to the MAO. Wait for availability announcement of agricultural subsidies or programs. Receive agricultural assistance or subsidies upon program approval. Detalye na Serbisyo Opisina ya Mangasiwa: Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) Klasipikasyon: Simple Paraan: in-person Oras na Panangproseso: Varies (depends on availability) Bayarin: Free (government-subsidized) Iner a Pag-aplayan: Municipal Agriculture Office, Poblacion Kontak: (075) 632-1873 Pinanlapuan: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Kaukolan a Na-update: August 2025 I-ulat so aliwan a tama ya impormasyon Na-scan a Dokumento Na-scan a pahina manipud ed opisyal a Mapandan Citizen’s Charter ya mangipabitar ed saray kinakailangan, bayarin, oras na panagproseso, tan responsable a staff para ed serbisyo. title: Aics
body: Social Welfare — IDs & Certifications AICS Assistance Apply for Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) in Mapandan. Learn about requirements, eligibility, and how to get help from the MSWDO. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "AICS Assistance", "description": "Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) is a government program that provides financial assistance to individuals and families facing emergencies such as medical crises, bereavement, or other unforeseen circumstances. In Mapandan, AICS assistance is administered by the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) in coordination with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD).", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Social Welfare — IDs & Certifications", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) is a government program that provides financial assistance to individuals and families facing emergencies such as medical crises, bereavement, or other unforeseen circumstances. In Mapandan, AICS assistance is administered by the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) in coordination with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD). Saray Kinakailangan Barangay certification stating the resident’s crisis situation Medical certificate (for medical-related assistance) Death certificate (for burial assistance) Valid government-issued ID Case study or social worker assessment Proseso Secure a barangay certification from your barangay captain or kagawad. Gather all required documents (medical certificate, death certificate, etc.). Visit the MSWDO office and submit your application with supporting documents. Wait for the social worker’s assessment and case study. Receive financial assistance upon approval of your application. title: Birth Certificate
body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Birth Certificate Request a birth certificate from the Mapandan MCR. Standard ₱115, late registration ₱315–₱1,015. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Birth Certificate", "description": "A birth certificate is a vital record issued by the Municipal Civil Registrar. Covers standard registration (₱115), registration by unmarried parents (₱215), hospital registration (₱100), and late registration (₱315–₱1,015 depending on age). Late registration requires 10-day posting period.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Civil Registry & Vital Records", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon A birth certificate is a vital record that serves as proof of identity, age, and Filipino citizenship. The Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) of Mapandan issues certified copies of locally registered birth certificates. This document is required for school enrollment, passport application, employment, and other legal purposes. Saray Kinakailangan Valid government-issued ID of the requesting party PSA copy of the birth certificate (if available, for verification) Barangay certification of residency (for the person named on the certificate) Affidavit of two disinterested persons (required for delayed registration only) Proseso Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office and present valid identification. Fill out the request form and provide the necessary supporting documents. Pay the certification fee at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Receive the certified birth certificate upon release. title: Building Permit
body: Building, Engineering & Zoning Building Permit Get a building permit from the Mapandan MEO. Simple: 3 days, Complex: 7 days, Highly Technical: 20 days per RA 11032. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Building Permit", "description": "A building permit is required under the National Building Code (PD 1096) and RA 11032. Processing times: Simple — 3 working days, Complex — 7 working days, Highly Technical — 20 working days. Includes site inspection, zoning and fire safety compliance.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Building, Engineering & Zoning", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon A building permit is a legal requirement under the National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096) for any construction, renovation, alteration, or demolition of a building or structure. The Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) of Mapandan reviews and issues building permits after ensuring compliance with safety standards, zoning, and structural requirements. Saray Kinakailangan Plans duly signed & sealed by licensed professionals Certified true copy of Tax Declaration (from Assessor Office) Xerox copy of land title (from Register of Deeds) Community Tax Certificate (from Treasury Office) Latest Tax receipts (from Treasury Office) Electrical & Sanitary permit (from Municipal Health Office) Confirmation of adjoining lot owners Certification from Barangay Captain Application for locational clearance (from Zoning Office) 2 Affidavits (from Notary Public) Affidavit of consent if not lot owner (from Notary Public) Fire Safety clearance (from BFP Office) Affidavit of adjoining lot owners Proseso Obtain a zoning clearance from the MPDC / Zoning Office. Prepare architectural and structural plans signed by licensed professionals. Submit all documents to the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) for review. Pay the building permit fees at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Receive the approved building permit after technical evaluation. Detalye na Serbisyo Opisina ya Mangasiwa: Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) Klasipikasyon: Highly Technical Paraan: in-person Oras na Panangproseso: 3 working days (Simple) / 7 working days (Complex) / 20 working days (Highly Technical) per RA 11032 Bayarin: Based on project cost (schedule per National Building Code) Iner a Pag-aplayan: Municipal Engineering Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Kontak: (075) 636-9382 / 0918-962-7423 Pinanlapuan: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Kaukolan a Na-update: August 2025 I-ulat so aliwan a tama ya impormasyon Na-scan a Dokumento Na-scan a pahina manipud ed opisyal a Mapandan Citizen’s Charter ya mangipabitar ed saray kinakailangan, bayarin, oras na panagproseso, tan responsable a staff para ed serbisyo. title: Business Permit
body: Business Permitting & Licensing New Business Permit Apply for a new business permit at the BPLO in Mapandan. Includes endorsement to Engineering, MPDC, RHU, and BFP. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "New Business Permit", "description": "A business permit is required for all individuals or entities intending to operate a commercial business within the Municipality of Mapandan. This permit is issued after compliance with documentary and safety requirements and upon payment of applicable fees.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Business Permitting & Licensing", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon A business permit is required for all individuals or entities intending to operate a commercial business within the Municipality of Mapandan. This permit is issued after compliance with documentary and safety requirements and upon payment of applicable fees. Saray Kinakailangan Filled up UNIFIED Form / Community Tax Certificate (from BPLO/Treasury Office) DTI/SEC/CDA Registration (from DTI/SEC/CDA Office or Online Application) BIR COR, if available (from RDO Calasiao) Barangay Clearance (System Integrated) Proseso Fill up the UNIFIED form and submit necessary requirements for verification (10 min). BPLO encodes data into the e-BPLS System. BPLO endorses applicant to various offices: Engineering (Occupancy Certificate), MPDC (Zoning Certificate), RHU (Health Certificate & Sanitary Permit), BFP (Fire Safety Inspection Certificate) (44 min). Pay fees and charges at the Treasury Office. Proceed to the Mayor's Office for issuance of Business Permit. Claim business plate and sticker at the Treasury Office (10 min). Detalye na Serbisyo Opisina ya Mangasiwa: Business Permit and Licensing Office (BPLO) Klasipikasyon: Simple Paraan: in-person Oras na Panangproseso: ~1 hour (10 min encoding + 44 min endorsement + 10 min pay & claim) Bayarin: Mayor's Permit (₱500–₱1,000) + Business Plate & Sticker (₱250) + Weights & Measure (₱100–200) + Storage Fee (₱550) + Garbage Fee (₱800–₱1,200) Iner a Pag-aplayan: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Kontak: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Pinanlapuan: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Kaukolan a Na-update: August 2025 I-ulat so aliwan a tama ya impormasyon Na-scan a Dokumento Na-scan a pahina manipud ed opisyal a Mapandan Citizen’s Charter ya mangipabitar ed saray kinakailangan, bayarin, oras na panagproseso, tan responsable a staff para ed serbisyo. title: Business Renewal
body: Business Permitting & Licensing Business Permit Renewal Renew your business permit at the BPLO in Mapandan. Annual renewal required to maintain compliance. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Business Permit Renewal", "description": "Businesses operating within Mapandan are required to renew their business permits annually. Renewal ensures that your business remains compliant with local regulations and avoids penalties for late filing.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Business Permitting & Licensing", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon Businesses operating within Mapandan are required to renew their business permits annually. Renewal ensures that your business remains compliant with local regulations and avoids penalties for late filing. Saray Kinakailangan Filled up UNIFIED Form / Community Tax Certificate (from BPLO/Treasury Office) DTI/SEC/CDA Registration (from DTI/SEC/CDA Office or Online Application) BIR COR (from RDO Calasiao) Barangay Clearance (System Integrated) Proseso Fill up the UNIFIED form and submit necessary requirements for verification (10 min). BPLO encodes data into the e-BPLS System. BPLO endorses applicant to Engineering, MPDC, RHU, and BFP for required certificates (44 min). Pay fees at the Treasury Office. Fees include Mayor's Permit, Business Tax (% of Gross Sales), Plate & Sticker, Weights & Measure, Storage Fee, and Garbage Fee. Proceed to the Mayor's Office for issuance of renewed Business Permit. Claim business plate and sticker at the Treasury Office. title: Cedula
body: Real Property & Revenue Cedula / Community Tax Certificate Get your Community Tax Certificate (cedula) in Mapandan. Individual: ₱5 + ₱1/₱1k; Juridical: ₱500 + ₱2/₱5k. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Cedula / Community Tax Certificate", "description": "The Community Tax Certificate (cedula) computation: Individual — ₱5.00 + ₱1.00 for every ₱1,000 gross income (not to exceed ₱5,000). Juridical — ₱500.00 + ₱2.00 for every ₱5,000 gross income (not to exceed ₱10,000). Interest of 24% per annum from March 1 to December 31.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Real Property & Revenue", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon The Community Tax Certificate (cedula) is computed as follows: Individual — ₱5.00 basic + ₱1.00 for every ₱1,000 gross income from business, profession, or property, but in no case shall exceed ₱5,000.00. Juridical — ₱500.00 basic + ₱2.00 for every ₱5,000 gross income from business or worth of real property, but in no case shall exceed ₱10,000.00. Interest of 24% per annum shall be imposed on individual or juridical securing their CTC from March 1 up to the end of the year. Saray Kinakailangan Old Community Tax Certificate (if available) Proof of income (if available) Proseso Go to Counters 1 and 2 and fill up the basic data form (15 min). Pay the required fees (3 min). Receive community tax certificate. Staff records in general collection system (2 min). Detalye na Serbisyo Opisina ya Mangasiwa: Municipal Treasury Office (MTO) Klasipikasyon: Simple Paraan: in-person Oras na Panangproseso: 20 minutes (15 min form filling + 3 min payment + 2 min recording) Bayarin: Individual: ₱5 + ₱1/₱1k income (max ₱5,000); Juridical: ₱500 + ₱2/₱5k income (max ₱10,000); 24% interest from March 1 Iner a Pag-aplayan: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Kontak: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Pinanlapuan: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Kaukolan a Na-update: August 2025 I-ulat so aliwan a tama ya impormasyon Na-scan a Dokumento Na-scan a pahina manipud ed opisyal a Mapandan Citizen’s Charter ya mangipabitar ed saray kinakailangan, bayarin, oras na panagproseso, tan responsable a staff para ed serbisyo. title: Health Consultation
body: Health Services Health Consultation Free health consultation at the Mapandan RHU. Walk-in service for all residents. 25 minutes per client. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Health Consultation", "description": "The Municipal Health Office (MHO) / Rural Health Unit (RHU) provides free health consultation services to all residents of Mapandan. This includes general medical consultations, health advice, and referrals to higher-level health facilities when necessary. Walk-in patients are served on a first-come, first-served basis.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Health Services", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon The Municipal Health Office (MHO) / Rural Health Unit (RHU) provides free health consultation services to all residents of Mapandan. This includes general medical consultations, health advice, and referrals to higher-level health facilities when necessary. Walk-in patients are served on a first-come, first-served basis. Saray Kinakailangan Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Proseso Register in Electronic Medical Record (EMR). Midwife registers new patients and encodes data. Classify patient: PhilHealth member (attach ID number) or non-PhilHealth member. Record consultation date, vital signs, and chief complaint. Occupy seats in waiting area and wait for name to be called. MHO check-up, assess, and treat the patient. Schedule follow-up check-up. Give available medicines to patient and encode. body: Real Property & Revenue Transfer of Land Ownership Transfer land ownership in Mapandan at the Assessor's Office. ₱150 recording fee, 30 minutes for Assessor processing. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Transfer of Land Ownership", "description": "Transfer of land ownership is the legal process of transferring property rights from one owner to another. Assessor cancels the old Tax Declaration and prepares the new one (10 min). Pay ₱150 recording fee at the Treasury Office. Claim the new Tax Declaration under the new owner's name (5 min). title: Name Correction
body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Name Correction (RA 9048) Correct your birth certificate under RA 9048. ₱3,000 for name change, ₱1,000 for clerical error. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Name Correction (RA 9048)", "description": "RA 9048 authorizes correction of clerical or typographical errors. Both require 10-day posting, MCR decision within 5 days, PSA processing 2–3 months.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Civil Registry & Vital Records", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon Republic Act No. 9048 authorizes the city or municipal civil registrar to correct clerical or typographical errors in civil registry entries without the need for a judicial order. This covers corrections in first names, nicknames, or minor spelling errors. This process does not apply to changes in gender, date of birth, or other substantive entries. Saray Kinakailangan Proof of Publication (from PSA) Certificate of Live Birth (from PSA) NBI Clearance Police Clearance (from PNP) Certificate of Employment (if employed) / Affidavit of non-employment Marriage Certificate, Medical records, SSS records, land title, baptismal certificate Proseso Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office and submit all required documents. File the petition for correction of clerical error. Pay the required fees at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Wait for the publication period to be completed. Basic 1% + SEF 1% of assessed value. 10%–20% discount for prompt/advance payment. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Real Property Tax Payment", "description": "Real property tax (RPT) is an annual tax on the assessed value of land, buildings, and improvements. Interest on unpaid real property tax: 2% per month but not to exceed 72%. Payment is processed at Counters 4-9 of the Treasury Office. title: Certificate Of Indigency
body: Social Welfare — IDs & Certifications Certificate of Indigency Get a Certificate of Indigency from the MSWDO for hospital discounts, legal aid, scholarships, and other social services. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Certificate of Indigency", "description": "A Certificate of Indigency is issued to indigent families certified by the Barangay Captain. It is used to avail of hospital discounts, legal assistance from PAO, scholarship assistance, and other social services.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Social Welfare — IDs & Certifications", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon The Certificate of Indigency is issued by the MSWDO to indigent families certified by the Barangay Captain. This document is required to avail of various services including hospital discounts, legal assistance from the Public Attorney's Office (PAO), scholarship assistance for college education, and other social welfare programs. The MSWDO conducts an interview and assessment to verify the client's eligibility before issuing the certificate. Saray Kinakailangan Barangay Certificate of Indigency Medical Certificate (if hospitalized) Police report / Police blotter / RTC/MTC report (if applicable) Report Card Form 138 / Recommendation (if for students) Birth Certificate (PSA/MCR) Proseso Register at the MSWD Office. title: Disaster Relief
body: Social Assistance & Protection Disaster Relief Assistance Disaster relief assistance for families affected by calamities in Mapandan. Relief goods and housing repair assistance available. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Disaster Relief Assistance", "description": "The MSWDO provides disaster relief assistance and rehabilitation services to families affected by floods, typhoons, fires, and other calamities. The service includes verification of affected families, distribution of relief goods through the Barangay Captain with the BDCC, and financial assistance (ESA) for families whose houses are totally destroyed. The MSWDO coordinates with the LGU, PSWDO, and DSWD Field Office I. Saray Kinakailangan Master list of affected families (from Barangay Captain) Barangay certificate Certificate of Indigency Proseso Report to the Barangay Captain the extent of damage. The Captain validates and forwards the list to MSWDO. MSWDO attends MDDC meeting conducted by the Local Chief Executive. MSWDO receives list of affected families and endorses to concerned social worker. Verification and inspection team (with Engineering, PNP, DSWD) assesses the damage. MSWDO requests and lobbies for allocation of relief goods from LGU, PSWDO, DSWD FO1. Distribution of relief goods through the Barangay Captain with the BDCC. For totally destroyed houses, MSWDO prepares project proposal for ESA funding. Financial assistance (ESA) is distributed to qualified beneficiaries. MSWDO monitors and evaluates project implementation for house repair/reconstruction. title: Nutrition Immunization
body: Health Services Nutrition & Immunization Program Free nutrition and immunization programs for children at the Mapandan RHU. Malnourishment intervention and NIP vaccines available. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Nutrition & Immunization Program", "description": "The RHU implements the Nutrition Program for malnourished children (0–59 months and older) and the National Immunization Program (NIP) for children against vaccine-preventable diseases.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Health Services", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon The RHU implements the Nutrition Program for malnourished children (0–59 months and older) and the National Immunization Program (NIP) for children against vaccine-preventable diseases. The nutrition program includes assessment, deworming, feeding with nutrient-dense food, and monthly monitoring. The immunization program administers age-appropriate vaccines after reviewing the child's records and checking vital signs. Saray Kinakailangan Birth Certificate (Municipal Civil Registry) Medical Records, Vaccination Records (from hospital of birth or pediatrician) Proseso For malnourished children (0–59 months): Barangay Nutrition Scholar assesses weight and height. Physician refers to RHU for deworming and medical intervention. Child is fed with nutrient-dense food (high carbohydrate and protein). Monthly monitoring of weight, height, and alertness. For immunization: BHW interviews child's information and reviews records. Midwife checks vital signs (weight and temperature). Midwife administers age-appropriate vaccine. Midwife advises parent on child care and expected outcome. Schedule next vaccination. body: Zoning & Planning Electrical Zoning Clearance Get an electrical zoning clearance from the MPDC in Mapandan. title: Professional Tax Receipt
body: Real Property & Revenue Professional Tax Receipt Get your Professional Tax Receipt at the Mapandan Treasury Office. ₱300 for professionals, ₱100 for non-professionals. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Professional Tax Receipt", "description": "A Professional Tax Receipt is required for all professionals exercising their profession. The fee is ₱300 for professionals (remitted to Provincial Treasury) and ₱100 for non-professionals.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Real Property & Revenue", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon A Professional Tax Receipt is required for all professionals exercising their profession in the Municipality of Mapandan. The fee is ₱300 for professionals (to be remitted to the Provincial Treasury Office) and ₱100 for non-professionals. Professionals must present their PRC ID, while non-professionals must present their Mayor's Permit. title: Birth Registration
body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Birth Registration Register a birth at the Mapandan MCR. Standard fee ₱115, late registration ₱315–₱1,015. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Birth Registration", "description": "Registration of birth with the Municipal Civil Registrar. Covers registration by attending midwife/hilot, unmarried parents, hospital administrators, and late registration with PSA verification.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Civil Registry & Vital Records", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon Registration of birth at the Municipal Civil Registrar. Covers three pathways: (1) Attending midwife/hilot reports child's birth — requires Marriage Certificate of parents and Mun. Form 102; (2) Unmarried parents — requires Community Tax Certificate; (3) Hospital administrator — requires Accomplished Mun. Form 102. Late registration requires negative PSA certification and supporting documents. Fees: Misc Fee ₱115 (standard), ₱215 (unmarried), ₱100 (hospital), ₱315–₱1,015 (late registration depending on age). Saray Kinakailangan Marriage Certificate of parents from PSA (for attending midwife/hilot registration) Community Tax Certificate from Treasury Office (for unmarried parents) Accomplished Mun. Call the hotline for immediate assistance. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "MDRRMO Rescue Operation & Emergency Medical Transport", "description": "The MDRRMO provides emergency rescue operations and medical transportation for residents of Mapandan during disasters, accidents, and medical emergencies. The service includes deployment of rescue teams and ambulance.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Disaster Risk Management", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon The MDRRMO provides 24/7 emergency rescue operations and medical transportation for residents of Mapandan. During disasters, accidents, and medical emergencies, the MDRRMO deploys its rescue teams and ambulance to respond to calls. The client or a family member contacts the MDRRMO hotline or reports in person. The MDRRMO assesses the situation, deploys the appropriate response team, and provides transportation to the nearest hospital if needed. Saray Kinakailangan No prior requirements needed for emergency response — call or report directly Proseso Call the MDRRMO hotline or report to the MDRRMO Office in case of emergency. Rescue team provides first aid, rescue operations, or medical transportation as needed. Patient or affected individuals are transported to the nearest hospital or safe location. title: Ldrrmo Transportation
body: Disaster Risk Management MDRRMO Standby / Transportation Request Request standby or transportation support from the MDRRMO for events and activities in Mapandan. This includes deployment of ambulances and rescue vehicles for large gatherings, sports events, and other activities. The requesting entity submits a letter of request specifying the event details and expected requirements. Saray Kinakailangan Letter of Request specifying event details, schedule, and venue Event permit or endorsement from the Mayor's Office (if applicable) Proseso Submit letter of request and event details to the MDRRMO Office. title: Youth Organization Registration
body: Youth Development Youth Organization Registration Program (YORP) Register your youth organization with the LYDO in Mapandan under the YORP. Free service, official recognition and program access. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Youth Organization Registration Program (YORP)", "description": "The Local Youth Development Office (LYDO) registers youth organizations in Mapandan under the Youth Organization Registration Program. Registration provides official recognition and access to LGU support, funding, and participation in youth programs.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Youth Development", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon The Local Youth Development Office (LYDO) administers the Youth Organization Registration Program (YORP) as mandated by the SK Reform Act (RA 11769). Registration provides official recognition of the youth organization, access to LGU support and funding opportunities, and participation in municipal, provincial, and national youth programs and activities. The LYDO assesses the application, verifies membership composition, and issues the Certificate of Registration. Saray Kinakailangan Letter of Intent to Register from the organization Constitution and By-Laws of the organization List of Officers and Members with ages (must be 15–30 years old) Minutes of the organization's founding meeting Endorsement from the Barangay Captain (if barangay-level organization) Proseso Submit the letter of intent and all required documents to the LYDO Office. LYDO staff receives and reviews the application (3 min). LYDO verifies the membership composition and constitution (3 min). LYDO prepares the Certificate of Registration (2 min). Receive the Certificate of Registration upon approval (2 min). title: Assessor Building Appraisal
body: Real Property & Revenue Building Appraisal / Assessment Get your building appraised and assessed by the Assessor's Office. ₱700 fee, 30 minutes processing. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Building Appraisal / Assessment", "description": "The Municipal Assessor's Office conducts appraisal and assessment of buildings and other structures for real property taxation. This includes new construction, renovation, and re-appraisal of existing buildings.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Real Property & Revenue", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Deskripsyon The Municipal Assessor's Office conducts appraisal and assessment of buildings and other structures for real property taxation purposes. The assessment covers the type of construction, floor area, materials used, depreciation, and current market value. The assessed value of the building is added to the land's assessed value for real property tax computation. The process includes review of building plans, site inspection, and computation of assessed value. Say Sangguniang Bayan—sakey a unicameral local legislative council—so mangipatupad na municipal legislative power. Pangulo to so Municipal Vice Mayor tan kaiba iray elected councilors tan ex-officio representatives na Liga ng mga Barangay tan Sangguniang Kabataan Federation. Makasaysayang Panlapuan Originally an agricultural barrio of Mangaldan referred to as balon baley ("new town"), Mapandan was first established as an independent pueblo pursuant to Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, promulgated by Governor General Emilio Bravo on December 28, 1887. Following population and fiscal losses caused by an epidemic in 1905 that temporarily reverted Mapandan to Mangaldan's jurisdiction, the municipality was re-established under American civil administration through Executive Order No. 10, signed by Governor General James F. Smith in 1909. No. 5, S-2024 Pipeline Legislative pipeline The legislative pipeline under the Local Government Code of 1991. 1 Filing A proposed ordinance is filed with the Sangguniang Bayan for consideration. 2 First Reading Initial reading and referral to the relevant committee for review. 3 Committee Hearing The committee holds hearings and deliberates on the proposal. 4 Committee Report Findings and recommendations are submitted back to the full council. 5 Second Reading Detailed floor discussion and debate on the proposed ordinance. 6 Third & Final Reading Final vote by the Sangguniang Bayan. 7 Mayor's Approval The Municipal Mayor reviews and approves the enacted ordinance. 8 Provincial Review Submitted to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Pangasinan for legal review under Sections 56 and 57 of R.A. 7160. 9 Posting & Effect The approved ordinance is posted publicly and takes effect across all 15 constituent barangays. Key Distinction Ordinance vs. Resolution Under the Local Government Code of 1991, the Sangguniang Bayan enacts two types of legislative measures: Ordinance A legislative measure that enacts a permanent rule or policy . Ordinances carry the force of law, create offices, levy taxes, or regulate conduct. They require three readings, publication, and the Mayor's approval (or passage by 2/3 override of a veto). Resolution A legislative measure that expresses the sentiment, intent, or opinion of the Sangguniang Bayan on a specific matter. Resolutions are used for internal housekeeping, requesting national action, or authorizing one-time transactions. They require only one reading and are not subject to publication.
